\textbf{1) federated inference is a promising approach to address data heterogeneity and privacy in real-world data applications; and 2) aligning local representations and learning a consensus graph in the global model can enhance federated inference performance.
we propose an approach to federated inference that aligns local representations and learns a consensus graph for global inference, and we demonstrate its effectiveness on real-life data sets.
\emph{we propose a federated inference framework for distributed heterogeneous data that aligns the local representations and learns a consensus graph to improve the global inference}.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three questions: (1) How to align the local data representations to enhance global inference? (2) How to learn the consensus graph to improve performance? (3) How to balance the local learning and global inference?
a more practical scenario of federated inference where data are partitioned into multiple parts, each part is owned by a different data owner, and each owner has a local data representation.

the following three contributions: 1) we propose a new framework for federated inference that is more realistic than the existing federated learning, 2) we introduce a novel approach to align the distributed representations, and 3) we learn a consensus graph to improve the performance of the global model.

the proposed method is a promising solution to federated inference.
the proposed framework can achieve a better performance than the baseline methods.

the proposed framework provides a novel and promising way for federated inference, where the local data owners can learn and use their own model, and a global consensus graph can be learned and used for better performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a framework that enables data owners to develop a common model collectively, and yet use it separately.
we propose a federated inference framework to learn a global model from multiple local models, and we show its effectiveness on four real-life applications.
we propose federated inference to address the distributed inference challenge in a federated setting, and we develop an effective approach for this purpose.

, by aligning local representations, we can learn a global model that is able to perform inference on distributed data parts, which is a step towards the ultimate goal of learning a global model from distributed data.
